cohort: 1543 neonates born between 24 and 34 weeks of gestation at the University Hospital of Udine from 2001 to 2019
finding: Preterm infants who received a complete course of betamethasone prophylaxis (24 mg) had a significantly lower prevalence of IVH, PVL, RDS, and higher Apgar scores compared to those who received a partial course (12 mg).
mod_finding: In single pregnancies, there was a higher prevalence of spontaneous vaginal deliveries in the incomplete CCS prophylaxis group and a higher prevalence of cesarean deliveries in the complete CCS prophylaxis group.
